comparison: Both evaluate activity against ESKAPE pathogens (C8, C9, C49-C53, C71). OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with clear demonstration through assays and MIC data. Peer review rates it UNCERTAIN due to concerns about heterologous expression system limitations and lack of purification controls (SDS-PAGE, carry-over controls). High agreement on claims addressed but divergent conclusions on evidence sufficiency.

Both evaluate increased prevalence and library comprehensiveness (C10, C54, C70). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED based on discovery of 12 new microcins. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, requesting better contextualization with existing software and previous distribution studies. Both identify need for additional validation but differ on current evidence strength.

Both evaluate therapeutic potential and antimicrobial applications (C11, C65, C67-C69, C72). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to speculative nature and need for in vivo validation. Peer review rates SUPPORTED, viewing the work as identifying promising antimicrobial candidates for future studies. Divergent perspectives on whether speculative claims are appropriately supported.

Both evaluate antimicrobial activity validation (C7, C44-C47). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with well-documented static inhibition assays and controls. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, requesting original images rather than presence/absence charts and clearer negative controls. Agreement on claims but disagreement on data presentation adequacy.

Both evaluate bioinformatic discovery and phylogenetic analysis (C4-C6, C28, C32, C34-C35). OpenEval finds methodology and phylogenetic support SUPPORTED. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN due to branches with <50% phylogenetic support and concerns about nucleotide alignment validity. Major disagreement on statistical validity of phylogenetic relationships.

OpenEval R1 addresses genomic organization and sequence conservation (C37-C43) as SUPPORTED. Peer R2 rates these claims UNCERTAIN, specifically challenging immunity protein identification (C37-C43) as lacking functional confirmation and being premature. Significant disagreement on immunity gene validation.

Both evaluate bioinformatic methodology (C73-C79). OpenEval finds detailed methodology SUPPORTED as part of comprehensive bioinformatic discovery. Peer review also rates methodology SUPPORTED with multiple reviewers confirming the bioinformatics analysis and experimental design are solid. Strong agreement on methodological soundness.

OpenEval R7 evaluates differential conservation and evolutionary hypothesis (C26-C27, C29-C31) as SUPPORTED. Peer R2 addresses sequence conservation (C26-C27) within context of immunity protein concerns but rates UNCERTAIN due to lack of functional validation. Partial overlap with different evaluation focuses.

Both evaluate heterologous expression system limitations (C56-C57). OpenEval rates therapeutic potential UNCERTAIN acknowledging native activity may differ. Peer review rates the experimental approach SUPPORTED, explicitly accepting the synthetic biology approach with appropriate caveats. Agreement on limitations but different evaluation targets (therapeutic claims vs. methodology).

OpenEval R2 evaluates antimicrobial activity including heterologous expression system (C80-C81) as SUPPORTED. Peer R6 specifically evaluates the heterologous expression approach (C81, C56-C57) as SUPPORTED with appropriate caveats. Agreement that the experimental design is valid despite limitations.

OpenEval R4 evaluates plant pathogen activity (C64) as SUPPORTED by experimental data. Peer R3 addresses antimicrobial validation including plant pathogens (C64) but rates UNCERTAIN due to lack of original images and unclear controls. Overlap on C64 with divergent conclusions on evidence presentation.

OpenEval R1 includes antiSMASH failure validation (C36) as part of SUPPORTED bioinformatic discovery. Peer R8 rates antiSMASH comparison (C36) as SUPPORTED, accepting the methodological justification. Agreement that custom approach was warranted.

OpenEval R1 includes plasmid localization (C33) as part of SUPPORTED bioinformatic findings. Peer R9 rates plasmid finding (C33) as SUPPORTED with high novelty, accepted without critique. Strong agreement on this novel observation.

OpenEval R8 evaluates scientific context and background claims (C1-C2, C12-C25, C66) as SUPPORTED by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background/context claims.
